title: Запредельное давление Шефа  (The Chef's Sky-High Blood Pressure)

segments.t: Outside by the dumpsters, Max is annoyed when Rodion Sergeyevich once again critiques his overcooked vegetables. Inside the office, meanwhile, a dizzy Chef Barinov has his blood pressure checked by a doctor, who assumes he has been drinking heavily—until Barinov groans that he went jogging instead.

Так вот, значит, компетентный человек шефа.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Oh, al dente vegetables again.' The meaning hinges on 'about' working together with 'dente' in spoken Russian. Vika answers right away.

'Just as overcooked as they were yesterday.' Notice how Russian expresses 'such' and 'yesterday' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Так вот, значит, компетентный человек шефа.
'So that is who the Chef's 'competent person' is.' Eleonora anchors the line on 'like this', while 'chef' completes the thought.
'And he has the nerve to lecture me.' In Russian, the idea of 'he' flows naturally into 'does' without extra filler words. Vika answers right away.
'About how I roast my meat.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'how' before landing on 'to fry'.
'Oh, I feel awful.' The grammar packs 'oh no' and 'bad' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Viktor Petrovich, you have been drinking again.' The meaning hinges on 'Viktor' working together with 'to drink' in spoken Russian. Vika answers right away.
'Your blood pressure is through the roof.' In Russian, the idea of 'by' flows naturally into 'blood pressure' without extra filler words.
'I have not been drinking.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'to drink'.
'Then what were you doing?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what' and finishing on 'did'. Vika answers right away.
'I would have been better off drinking.' In Russian, the idea of 'better' flows naturally into 'to drink' without extra filler words.
'Viktor Petrovich.' In Russian, the idea of 'Viktor' flows naturally into 'Petrovich' without extra filler words.
'Tomorrow I am going jogging again.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'tomorrow' before landing on 'will run'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.

Так вот, значит, компетентный человек шефа.
